transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’m here because my eating has felt a little out of control lately. Not all the time, but some evenings after work—especially if I’ve been really “good” or strict during the day—I end up eating much more than I meant to.

It might be dinner, and then cereal, crackers, leftovers… maybe sweets too, all within a couple of hours. I feel kind of embarrassed saying that, but I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
Do you ever make yourself vomit or use laxatives after one of these episodes of eating more than you meant to?

I… I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I don’t think it’s, um, a regular thing I do or anything. I feel pretty ashamed after, but I don’t know if I’d say I have a pattern with vomiting or laxatives.

Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
How often do these episodes of eating more than you meant to happen?

It’s… probably most weeks, if I’m being honest. Not every day or anything, but maybe one or two nights in a week where I eat a lot more than I meant to.

And then the next day I usually try to sort of balance it out—like skipping a meal or exercising longer. I know that may not be the best way to handle it, but… that’s what I’ve been doing.
Do you worry about gaining weight as a result of these episodes of eating more than you meant to?

Yes… I do worry about gaining weight after those nights. I try not to make a big deal out of it, but the next day I’ll kind of tell myself I’m just “getting back on track.”

So I might skip breakfast and lunch, or I’ll take an extra-long hike, or push harder at softball conditioning even if I’m tired. It feels like I’m making up for it, I guess… if that makes sense.
How often do you skip meals or exercise to make up for eating more than you meant to?

Um… I’d say it’s been happening most weeks lately. For the past few months, usually there’ll be one or two nights where I eat way more than I meant to, and then the next day I try to make up for it.

I don’t always call it “skipping meals,” I guess—I’ll tell myself I’m just being careful or getting back on track—but it can be skipping breakfast or lunch, or exercising longer than I normally would. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you ever used laxatives after one of these episodes of eating more than you meant to?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, that’s not really something I’ve done after eating too much.

I mostly just try to be careful the next day, but I haven’t used laxatives for that. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating more than you meant to?
No… I mean, I don’t make myself throw up after that. I know that’s something people ask about, and it’s kind of embarrassing to even talk about, but no, that’s not something I do.
How many days a week do you try to make up for eating more than you meant to by skipping meals or exercising more?

Usually maybe one or two days a week… I mean, it’s not every day. It’s more like if I have one or two nights where I eat way more than I planned, then the next day I’ll try to “balance it out” by skipping a meal or exercising longer.

That’s been happening most weeks for the past few months, I guess. Does that make sense?
Do you try to make up for eating more than you meant to every time it happens?

Not every single time, no… or at least I try not to think of it that way. But a lot of the time, the next day I’ll tell myself I’m just getting back on track, like skipping breakfast and lunch or taking a longer hike than usual.

Sometimes with softball conditioning I’ll push harder too, even if I’m tired. I guess in my head I’m sort of “making up for it,” but I don’t know if that counts every time.
Do you try to make up for eating more than you meant to by skipping meals or exercising more every week?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but for the past few months it’s been most weeks. Usually there’ll be one or two nights where I eat way more than I meant to, and then the next day I’ll try to sort of “fix it” by skipping meals or exercising longer.

It’s not every day or anything, but… yeah, most weeks.
Do you try to make up for eating more than you meant to every single week?

Pretty much every week, yes… I don’t love saying that, but for the past few months it’s been most weeks. Usually it’s like one or two nights where I eat way more than I meant to, and then the next day I try to make up for it by skipping meals or exercising longer.

Not every day, but… yes, most weeks.
Do you try to make up for eating more than you meant to by skipping meals or exercising more at least three days a week?

I don’t think it’s usually three days a week, no. It’s more like… most weeks, there might be one or two nights where I eat way more than I meant to, and then the next day I’ll try to make up for it by skipping meals or exercising longer.

So it does happen regularly, but I wouldn’t want to say three days every week if that’s not accurate.
Do you try to make up for eating more than you meant to by skipping meals or exercising more at least one day a week?

Yes… at least one day a week, that would be fair to say. I don’t think it’s, like, constant, but for the past few months it’s been most weeks. Usually I’ll have one or two nights where I eat way more than I meant to, and then the next day I try to make up for it by skipping meals or exercising longer.
Do you have these episodes of eating more than you meant to at least once a week?

Yes… I think at least once a week is accurate. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but for the past few months it’s been most weeks—usually one or two nights where I end up eating way more than I planned.
Do you usually feel like you can't stop eating or control how much you're eating during those episodes?

Yes… I think that’s probably true. I don’t like saying it that way, but once I get started on those nights, I keep going back to the kitchen even while I’m telling myself I should stop.

It’s not like I’m trying to be out of control, but I don’t really feel back in charge until I’m already uncomfortably full, if that makes sense.
Do you try to make up for eating more than you meant to by skipping meals or exercising more on the same day it happens?

Usually it’s more the next day, not always the same day. Like after one of those nights, I’ll tell myself I’m just “getting back on track,” and I might skip breakfast and lunch, or take a really long hike, or push harder at softball conditioning even if I’m tired.

I know that probably counts as making up for it… I just try to frame it like I’m being disciplined, I guess.
Do you try to make up for eating more than you meant to by skipping meals or exercising more almost every day?

Not almost every day, no. I mean… I do it after one of those nights. The next day I’ll tell myself I’m making up for it, or “getting back on track,” and I might skip breakfast and lunch, or take an extra-long hike, or push harder at softball conditioning even if I’m tired.

But it’s not every day. It’s more tied to when I’ve overeaten, if that answers it right.
Do you try to make up for eating more than you meant to by skipping meals or exercising more every single day that it happens?

Yes… I mean, if it happens that night, then the next day I usually do try to make up for it somehow. I’ll tell myself I’m just getting back on track, but it can be skipping breakfast and lunch, or doing an extra-long hike, or pushing harder at softball conditioning even if I’m already tired.

I know that sounds like I’m compensating… I guess I just don’t like to call it that.
Do you try to make up for eating more than you meant to by skipping meals or exercising more after every single episode of overeating?

After every single time… I think, yes, pretty much. I don’t always do it right that minute, but the next day I’ll try to “make up for it,” if that makes sense.

Usually that means I’ll skip breakfast and lunch, or I’ll take a really long hike, or push myself harder at softball conditioning even if I’m tired. I try to tell myself it’s just being disciplined, but… yeah, it’s usually after one of those nights.
Do you try to make up for eating more than you meant to by skipping meals or exercising more after almost every episode of overeating?

Yes… almost every time, I think. Not in a dramatic way, or at least I don’t mean it to be, but the next day I’ll kind of tell myself I’m making up for it.

Usually I’ll skip breakfast and lunch, or I’ll go for an extra-long hike, or push harder at softball conditioning even when I’m tired. I tell myself it’s just getting back on track, but… yes, it’s usually after those episodes.
